entries.title: Pathways v2: Journeys, People matching, Content Gaps, and restructured navigation
entries.summary: Pathways gains a full **Journeys** module — create, publish, review, approve, and send back journeys from **Pathways → Journeys**. **CRM People v2** adds relationship filtering, match review, link/unlink with undo, and an explain view. **Topics** now supports credit mapping, a **Content Gaps** tab, topic briefs, and the ability to undo a credit decision. **Settings → Privacy & Value** adds a consent log, accredited credit types, and permission-gated value preview. The sidebar is restructured: Pathways splits into **Overview / Journeys / Configure**, CMS is renamed **Publish**, **Content Gaps** appears as its own entry, and **Marketing → Newsletters** is added.

enable.path: Ask your Customer Success Manager to enable Pathways; then Pathways → Journeys

where.path: Pathways → Overview / Journeys / Configure; Topics → Content Gaps; Settings → Privacy & Value

entries.use_case: Organizations running structured learning or certification programs can now build and publish Journeys, review topic credit decisions, identify content gaps in their library, and manage consent and accredited credit types — all within Pathways, without leaving Sessionboard.

cs_action.note: Pathways v2 endpoints and nav are live but the feature requires org-level enablement. The Home and Apps modules added in this PR are staff-only and should not be shown to customers.

internal.when_to_bring_up: A customer asks about learning pathways, credit mapping, content gap analysis, or managing a speaker pipeline across events.
internal.who_should_get_it: Organizations with Pathways (beta) enabled that run accredited programs, multi-event content strategies, or structured speaker development.
internal.staff_path: Pathways → Overview / Journeys / Configure; Topics → Content Gaps; Settings → Privacy & Value. Home and Apps (Connected) are staff-only modules — do not surface to customers.
internal.gotchas: Recap setup, /my public token routes, and Webinars endpoints are not yet implemented — the UI shows 'not available yet'. Sync alerts store the preference but do not send email. Saved source settings are not yet read by sync jobs. Some response fields (review evidence, brief, gap prose, consent log source, Results labels) are plain English text rendered as-is by the UI.
internal.talk_track: Pathways v2 gives your team a single place to build Journeys, map credits to topics, spot content gaps before your next event, and maintain a consent log for accredited programs — all connected to the contacts and sessions you already manage in Sessionboard.

draft.docs_gap: The Pathways overview guide should be expanded to cover Journeys (create, publish, review workflow), the People v2 match/link/unlink flow, Content Gaps, the Privacy & Value settings panel (consent log, accredited credit types, value preview), and the restructured sidebar navigation introduced in v2.
draft.why_use_it: Pathways helps organizations manage the full lifecycle of professional development content — from collecting and reviewing session topics to mapping credits, identifying gaps, and guiding participants through structured Journeys. Use it when you need to connect your event content to learning outcomes, accreditation requirements, or audience development goals across multiple events.

entries.title: Pathways v2: Journeys, People, Content, Pulse, Webinars, and member-facing My Pathway screens
entries.summary: The **Pathways** module has been rebuilt end-to-end. Organizers now have access to: a **Journeys** list and individual journey pages; a **Review queue** (deep-linkable by group); **Results**, **Setup**, **Pulse**, **Library**, **Sponsors**, and **Webinars** screens (series and follow-ups); a **CRM People v2** directory with per-person graph profile tabs and a **Match review** workspace; **Content** screens including **Topics**, a topic page, a review workspace, and **Content Gaps**; an event-level **Pathways** dashboard, **Recap setup** (under **Program → After the event**), and a **Repurpose** run page. Members can access their personal pathway at **/my** and **/my/:token**. Navigation is server-driven; sidebar icons for newsletters, auto-renew, and mark-email-read are now resolved correctly.

enable.path: Ask your Customer Success Manager to enable Pathways v2; then Pathways → Journeys

where.path: Pathways → Journeys (org); Program → After the event → Recap (event)

entries.use_case: Use Pathways v2 to guide attendees through a structured learning or engagement journey before, during, and after an event — tracking their progress, surfacing content gaps, and giving each member a personalised /my page showing their pathway status.

cs_action.note: Several endpoints are not yet live (Recap setup GET/PUT, /my public token reads, Webinar series/follow-ups). Those pages show a 'not available yet' card rather than an error, but CSMs should confirm which surfaces are fully functional before demoing to customers. The Home and Graph lens pages are currently staff-only or gated by advanced_search — do not surface to customers yet. The Sync alerts toggle says 'We'll email you' but the server does not send emails yet; soften or hide that string before GA.

internal.when_to_bring_up: When a customer asks how to keep attendees engaged between events, build content journeys, or track individual learning progress.
internal.who_should_get_it: Customers on the Pathways beta who want structured attendee journeys and post-event content repurposing.
internal.staff_path: Pathways → Journeys; event sidebar → Pathways dashboard; Program → After the event → Recap
internal.gotchas: Recap setup, /my member pages, and Webinar series screens are UI-complete but backed by missing API endpoints — they render a 'not available yet' card. Home and Graph lens are staff/advanced_search gated and must not be shown to customers. Sync alert emails are not yet sent by the server despite the UI toggle.
internal.talk_track: Pathways v2 gives your attendees a personalised journey — before, during, and after the event — with a /my page they can return to, and gives your team a Pulse dashboard and Content Gaps view to see where engagement drops off.

draft.docs_gap: The /pathways/overview article should be expanded to cover the Journeys list, Review queue, Pulse dashboard, Content Gaps, Recap setup, Webinars screens, the CRM People v2 directory with Match review, and the member-facing /my pathway page.
draft.why_use_it: Pathways turns a one-time event into an ongoing engagement programme. Organizers build journeys that connect sessions, content, webinars, and sponsors into a coherent sequence, then track each person's progress through a unified People directory and Pulse dashboard. Members get a personalised portal at /my where they see their goals, topics, and channel preferences — giving them a reason to stay engaged long after the event ends.

entries.title: Record comments and @mentions are now restricted to the organizing team
entries.summary: Comments posted on sessions, contacts, groups, and tasks no longer notify or @mention evaluators, speakers, or users from other organizations. The **@mention suggestions** list now shows only accepted team members with org access, and notification recipients for new comments and replies are filtered to the organizing team only.

where.path: Sessions / Contacts / Groups / Tasks → a record → Comments

entries.use_case: Organizers can leave internal notes and @mention teammates on any record without risk of accidentally notifying a reviewer, speaker, or user from another organization. Comment threads stay within the organizing team.

internal.when_to_bring_up: A customer reports that evaluators or speakers received unexpected internal comment notifications, or asks why reviewers were appearing in @mention suggestions.
internal.who_should_get_it: All customers who use record comments or @mentions on sessions, contacts, groups, or tasks.
internal.staff_path: Sessions / Contacts / Groups / Tasks → a record → Comments → @mention suggestions dropdown
internal.gotchas: Custom roles cloned from the Evaluator role carry no evaluator marker and are treated as team members — they will still appear in @mention suggestions and receive notifications. This is a known limitation shared with the related messaging/notes fix in #4478.
internal.talk_track: Internal comments on records are now scoped to the organizing team only — evaluators and speakers will not appear in @mention suggestions and will not receive comment notifications.

draft.docs_gap: The guide should note that @mention suggestions and comment notifications are restricted to accepted organizing team members and do not include evaluators, speakers, or portal users.
